input.question: The history in the U.S. behind the adoption of the DD bra size
input.ground_truth: Hey there! I'm one of the bra fitting nazis over at /r/ABraThatFits, the community that produced that post you linked to, so I re-asked your question over there [and got some good answers if you want to check them out!](_URL_0_) It was super weird to see two of my favorite subreddits collide like this. Overall, however, there is not a lot of scholarship on the evolution of bras and bra sizing, which is sad, and I could probably spin you a nice little rant about sexism in academia, but I'm sure you can fill it in yourself. :) FYI, there isn't too much resistance in American brands against letters past D. No one does DDDD. Victoria's Secret goes D, DD, DDD, but lots of brands go D, DD, F, G, or D, DD, G, H. Take a look at two major US makers, Wacoal and Goddess, for examples of non-D sizing terminology. Lane Bryant, a major supplier of DD+ bras also does letters other than D. It's mostly just highly inconsistent, unlike the UK which has its stuff together.

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

I am a woman.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: The history in the U.S. behind the adoption of the DD bra size

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a special measuring tape for your chest, just like you have one for your waist. A long time ago, people who made bras used letters like A, B, C, D, and so on to show how big someone’s chest was. But sometimes, the letters didn’t fit everyone. 

When people noticed that some grown-up women’s chests were even bigger than what the letter C could show, they needed a new letter. So, they made a new letter called “D.” This helped more women find bras that fit them better.

But here’s something interesting: the company that made the measuring tape for bras (called the Bra Size Measurement Guide) used to say that the letter D was for very big chests. But some people thought the way they measured was not fair or right. For a while, some people even thought the letter D didn’t exist, but it really does! 

So, the story behind the DD bra size is that people wanted to make sure everyone could find a bra that fits, even if they are a little bigger, and that’s why they added the D and even DD sizes.
